name: Bioethics
notes: Six courses; fulfills the humanities academic division of the Rochester Curriculum.
Students may major, OR minor, OR complete a cluster within the public health-related programs - not more than one.
NO MORE THAN ONE COURSE may overlap between a public health minor and another program of study (stricter than the University's usual two-course cap).
MHB 210 was valid only until fall 2023; MHB 410U begins spring 2025; the MHB 4xxU courses are open to juniors and seniors.

requirementGroups.label: Introduction to Public Health
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Required Courses. PHLT 101: Introduction to Public Health I

requirementGroups.label: Medical or public health ethics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Plus one of the following: PHIL 225: Ethical Decisions in Medicine; PHIL 228: Public Health Ethics

requirementGroups.label: Two bioethics courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: At least two of the following: PHLT 236: Healthcare and Law; PHLT 300W: Seminar in Bioethics; PHIL 225: Ethical Decisions in Medicine (if not taken above); PHIL 228: Public Health Ethics (if not taken above); PHIL 312: Neuroethics; PHIL 313: Global Health Ethics (prerequisite: one PHIL); PHIL 321: Death; MHB 210: Bioethics at the Bedside (valid until fall 2023); MHB 410U: Clinical Ethics (valid beginning spring 2025; open to juniors and seniors); MHB 472U: Philosophical Foundations of Bioethics (open to juniors and seniors)

requirementGroups.label: Two further ethics electives
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: May take up to two of the following: MHB 420U: Stories in Healthcare: Clinicians, Patients, and Narrative Medicine OR MHB 430U: Visual Arts in Healthcare (open to juniors and seniors); PHIL 102: Ethics; PHIL 103: Contemporary Moral Problems; PHIL 220/220W: Recent Ethical Theory; PHIL 223/223W: Social and Political Philosophy; PHIL 226: Philosophy of Law; PHIL 230/230W: Environmental Justice
requirementGroups.note: The page caps this list at two courses; a student who takes more bioethics courses above needs fewer here.
